title: Bottles and Breastfeeding Equipment Screening Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the House on September 20, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Bottles and Breastfeeding Equipment Screening Act

(Sec. 2) This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to:

  • notify air carriers, TSA security screening personnel, and private security screening personnel of TSA's 3-1-1 Liquids Rule Exemption guidelines allowing baby formula, breast milk, purified deionized water for infants, and juice on airlines; and
  • include training on all special screening procedures for TSA security screening personnel and private security screening personnel.

summary.headline: A 2016 law requires the TSA to tell airlines and screeners about rules that let travelers with baby formula, breast milk, infant water, and juice bring those liquids through security.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Transportation Security Administration to notify air carriers and both TSA and private security screeners about its guidelines exempting baby formula, breast milk, purified deionized water for infants, and juice from the usual 3-1-1 liquids limits. It also requires that screener training cover all special screening procedures for these items.

who_it_affects.group: Parents and caregivers traveling with infants or young children
who_it_affects.how: They are meant to have clearer, more consistent guidance on bringing baby formula, breast milk, infant water, and juice through airport security.
The law supports screening procedures that cover breast milk and breastfeeding equipment during airport checkpoint screening.
